The July release says "Net debt to Adjusted EBITDA of 3.5-times" (page:2). The MD&A reports the covenant-related measure "Net debt to EBITDA – excluding restructuring and other costs" at 3.5 times (page:59). The names differ and the MD&A defines its measure in section 11.1. The facility definitions are not supplied, so the exact covenant calculation cannot be verified. - Segment structure. facts.label: Analytical read-through
facts.text: - Usable coverage: three interim sources (September 30, 2025 statements; March 31, 2026 statements; June 30, 2026 MD&A) plus the fourth quarter 2025 and 2026 releases give a continuous quarterly record. The December 31, 2025 statement of financial position is available as a comparative in the March 2026 statements (page:1 and page:2) and the MD&A (page:50 and page:51). The MD&A eight-quarter table covers each quarter of 2025 and 2026. - Strongest contrary evidence: the audited annual layer is missing, and the latest quarter contains events that change the credit picture. The July release reports a net loss driven by an impairment relating to TELUS Digital and a dividend reset to support deleveraging. Management also states the leverage target date moved to year-end 2028. These are management claims in a release, and the MD&A is the filed document that carries the figures. - Source risk mechanism, evidence to risk to consequence. First, evidence: the Form 40-F text incorporates its financial statements by reference from an exhibit not in the pack. Risk: an analyst could mistake the cover document for the annual report and treat full-year 2025 figures as audited. Consequence: CP-1 must label fiscal year 2025 as assembled from quarterly sources, and CP-5 must not treat quarterly sums as audited. Second, evidence: debt by series, maturities and the facility table are in the March 2026 notes, while the June 2026 MD&A gives only movements and totals. Risk: the refinancing schedule and series list are one quarter old, and the quarter had redemptions, a note reclassified to current and growth in commercial paper. Consequence: CP-2 can state liquidity at June 30, 2026 but must date the maturity schedule at March 31, 2026. Third, evidence: junior subordinated notes get partial equity credit in the leverage measure, and covenant definitions are not supplied. Risk: reported leverage and covenant leverage may differ from a gross-debt view. Consequence: CP-1 and CP-2 must show each definition and carry the gap instead of assuming headroom from the reported ratio. - What cannot proceed: verification of covenant calculations against agreement definitions; guarantor-level or restricted-group analysis; a series-by-series debt schedule at June 30, 2026; audited full-year 2025 tie-outs; any event after July 31, 2026. - Next evidence action: supply Exhibit 99.4 and Exhibit 99.3 of the Form 40-F, the Exhibit 99.1 interim statements that accompany the June 30, 2026 MD&A, the credit agreements and indentures, a rating-agency source, and any filing between July 31, 2026 and November 5, 2026.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: TELUS is a large, investment-grade-rated Canadian telecommunications issuer whose reported leverage is 3.5 times net debt to EBITDA excluding restructuring and other costs at June 30, 2026, above both its previous and its newly set objective ranges, but below the covenant limit of 4.25 times. The financial base can be built from the pinned sources for the latest quarter and for four consecutive balance sheet dates, with limits. Reported leverage depends on a definition that gives half equity credit to the junior subordinated notes and adjusts for hedging items, so a gross view is also shown: total debt, including lease liabilities and short-term borrowings, is 4.30 times LTM EBITDA excluding restructuring and other costs. Cash interest cover on the same EBITDA is 4.62 times, down from 5.09 times a quarter earlier, partly because cash interest paid in Q2 2026 included a prepayment premium. Liquidity at June 30, 2026 is cash and temporary investments of 1,387, revolver availability of 657 after a 2,093 commercial paper backstop, securitization availability of 680 and a further 344 on a non-revolving bank facility due June 2027. Current maturities of long-term debt are 3,802. The second quarter brought a 2,135 impairment relating to TELUS Digital, a net loss of 1,830, a dividend reset and lower guidance. The view is restricted by missing audited FY2025 statements, missing second-quarter notes and missing agreements, so FY2025 flows are assembled from quarters and the debt register is dated March 31, 2026. All figures below are C$ millions unless stated.

facts.label: Definitions review
facts.text: - EBITDA is operating revenues and other income less goods and services purchased and employee benefits expense [MDA2Q26 page:81 "EBITDA as calculated by TELUS is equivalent to Operating revenues and other income less the total of Goods and services purchased expense and Employee benefits expense"]. It includes restructuring and other costs; impairment is added back in the segment reconciliation, so EBITDA is stated before impairment [REL2Q26 page:20]. - EBITDA excluding restructuring and other costs is the leverage and coverage numerator. In Q2 2026 and every quarter in the eight-quarter table it equals Adjusted EBITDA [REL2Q26 page:20 "EBITDA – excluding restructuring and other costs and Adjusted EBITDA 1,639"]. Adjusted EBITDA excludes items the issuer considers unusual [MDA2Q26 page:81]. - Net debt is long-term debt less the junior subordinated notes equity credit, plus debt issuance costs, less hedging derivative and accumulated other comprehensive income items, less cash, plus short-term borrowings [Q1FS page:7 "TELUS Corporation junior subordinated notes equity credit deducted in calculating net debt"]. For the equity credit, "only one-half of the principal of our junior subordinated notes is included as debt" [MDA2Q26 page:57]. The net debt components at June 30, 2026 are not printed in the pinned sources because they sit in the unsupplied Note 3. - Net interest cost is financing costs adjusted for pension net interest, capitalized interest, debt-purchase gains and virtual power purchase agreement items [MDA2Q26 page:85]. It is an accrual measure, not cash interest. - Covenants: leverage must not exceed 4.25 to 1.00 and coverage must not be less than 2.00 to 1.00 at each quarter-end; the reported ratios at June 30, 2026 are 3.5 and 4.9, and "There are certain minor differences in the calculation" against the management measures [MDA2Q26 page:61]. The Q1FS describes the second test as an operating cash flow to interest expense ratio [Q1FS page:43 "our operating cash flow to interest expense ratio must not be less than 2.00:1.00"]. The credit agreement definitions are not supplied. - Objective range changed. In Q1FS the objective range is 2.2 to 2.7 times [Q1FS page:8 "Our long-term objective range for this ratio is 2.2 – 2.7 times"]. The June 2026 MD&A shows 2.5 to 3.0 times, with an objective of about 3.0 times in 2028 [MDA2Q26 page:27 "Net debt to EBITDA – excluding restructuring and other costs ratio of 2.5 to 3.0 times"]. Comparisons to the objective must name the vintage. - Free cash flow is the issuer's non-GAAP measure and excludes certain working capital changes, proceeds from divested assets and other items [MDA2Q26 page:83 "Free cash flow: We report this measure"]. It is not a covenant measure.

facts.label: Interpretation: evidence, mechanism, implication
facts.text: - Leverage is definition-dependent. Evidence: net debt of 25,963 uses half equity credit for junior subordinated notes and EBITDA of 7,315. Mechanism: the notes are subordinated and carry a rating-event repurchase at 102 per cent, so the equity credit depends on agency treatment; if lost, reported leverage rises toward the gross figure. Implication: senior creditors should monitor the gross ratio of 4.30 times as well as the covenant ratio, because covenant headroom is 0.70 times on the issuer's own definition. - Cash interest cover is moving down. Evidence: EBITDA over cash interest paid fell from 5.31 at FY2025 to 4.62 at June 30, 2026. Mechanism: interest paid rose by 142 in Q2 2026 and 201 in H1 2026 on 2025 junior subordinated issuance, the promissory note and the prepayment premium, while LTM EBITDA excluding restructuring and other costs fell from 7,354 to 7,315. Implication: cash cover has less margin, although part of the Q2 2026 rise is one-off. - Refinancing and liquidity. Evidence: current maturities of long-term debt of 3,802, commercial paper of 2.1 billion fully backstopped by a revolver with 657 availability. Mechanism: commercial paper is classified as current but is supported by the revolver, so it consumes revolver capacity one for one and the availability of 657 is what remains after that backstop. The other current maturities, including the US$600 million 2.80% notes reclassified to current and the Series CZ balance paid in July 2026, rely on cash of 1,387, securitization availability of 680, non-revolving availability of 344 or new issuance. Implication: near-term maturities depend on commercial paper rollover and market access; the investment-grade wording supports access but ratings are not supplied and not tested here. - Earnings quality. Evidence: Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of 1,777 versus 1,812 and a 2,135 non-cash impairment; Digital Adjusted EBITDA 72 versus 89. Mechanism: the impairment does not affect EBITDA or covenants, which are not impacted by revaluation of goodwill [MDA2Q26 page:61 "The covenants are not impacted by revaluation"], but signals lower recoverable value in the TELUS Digital unit. Implication: covenant headroom is unaffected by the impairment, while the lower guidance affects forward leverage. - Dividend reset. Evidence: dividends paid 864 in H1 2026 against free cash flow of 1,128 in the same half. Mechanism: the quarterly dividend falls from 0.4184 to 0.1875 per share. Implication: management cites this as a deleveraging lever; the 2.7 billion saving through 2028 is a management estimate.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: TELUS Corporation is a British Columbia company and one of Canada's largest telecommunications groups, with three reporting segments: TELUS technology solutions (mobile, fixed data and voice, security and automation, agriculture and consumer goods technology), TELUS Health (employee and family assistance programs, benefits administration, virtual care) and TELUS Digital (digital solutions, AI and data, trust and safety, customer experience management). The sources describe no controlling shareholder, no sponsor and no pending change of control; ownership detail beyond the share count and a Canadian-ownership voting restriction is not supplied. The creditor-relevant structure is a parent that issues all identified senior notes, commercial paper and junior subordinated notes and is effectively subordinated to obligations of, or guaranteed by, its subsidiaries, with a subsidiary (Terrion) holding minority outside equity. The relevant history is a 2025 reshaping of the perimeter: the acquisition of Workplace Options in May 2025, the establishment of Terrion in July 2025 with outside equity, and the buy-in of the TELUS Digital minority on October 31, 2025, followed in 2026 by a 2,135 impairment of TELUS Digital, a management transition, a dividend reset, lower guidance and asset sale processes. Business risk is anchored by a large mobile and fibre base with declining ARPU at a decelerating rate, partly offset by growth in connected devices and internet connections. As an analyst reading, TELUS Digital depends on external clients and intersegment work, and Health earnings were built partly by acquisition. The view is restricted by the absence of the annual information form, the transaction agreements and any filing after July 31, 2026.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: TELUS is not the subject of a sponsor buyout, merger or refinancing in the pinned sources, so no deal-level use of proceeds, sponsor or closing condition applies; one Insufficient Information row stands for any transaction after July 31, 2026, which is Not supplied. The completed transactions that shape the creditor's perimeter are these. First, the TELUS Digital privatization: on June 12, 2025 TELUS Corporation submitted a non-binding indication of interest to the board of TELUS International (Cda) Inc. [Q3FS page:63 "submitted a non-binding indication of interest"], signed a definitive agreement on September 2, 2025 at "for a price per share of US$4.50" [Q3FS page:64 "for a price per share of US$4.50"], payable in cash, Common Shares or a combination subject to a 25 per cent cap on shares, and closed on October 31, 2025 [Q3FS page:64 "The transaction closed October 31, 2025"]. The final cash and share mix and the cash outlay are Not supplied in the pinned sources. Second, Terrion: a wireless tower infrastructure partnership established on July 24, 2025 that issued equity to an outside holder for net cash proceeds of 1,246 [Q3FS page:65 "Net cash proceeds $ 1,261"], after which TELUS keeps 50.1 per cent voting and economic interest and holds a call option exercisable in whole in September 2027 if there is a partner dispute or after September 2057 at generally the greater of fair value and a multiple on invested capital [Q3FS page:64 "call option"]. The outside holder is not named in the pinned sources. The Terrion non-controlling interest was 792 at September 30, 2025 and non-controlling interests were 808 at June 30, 2026 (CP-1). Third, Workplace Options: TELUS acquired 100 per cent on May 1, 2025 [Q3FS page:44 "On May 1, 2025, we acquired 100% of Workplace Options"], with cash consideration of 453 funded in part by 280 (US$200 million) of preferred shares issued by a subsidiary to a private equity investor; the preferred shares were later exchanged for a US$200 million promissory note and the note was repaid in Q2 2026 with a prepayment premium of 51 (CP-1). Fourth, liability management: tender offers in June and December 2025 that bought back senior notes (series CL, CU, CW, CAB, CAE and U.S. dollar notes), with gains on purchase of long-term debt of 222 in Q3 2025 and 81 in Q4 2025 [MDA2Q26 page:29 "Gain on purchase of long-term debt"], the full redemption of the 3.75% Series CV notes on January 16, 2026, the redemption of 500 of the 2.75% Series CZ notes on May 8, 2026, and the payment of the remaining 300 of that series at maturity after June 30, 2026 (CP-1). Fifth, equity and distributions: the dividend reset announced July 31, 2026 and the end of the dividend reinvestment plan discount effective October 1, 2026 [REL2Q26 page:4 "representing a reset of 55 per cent to an annualized amount of $0.75 per share"]; no shares were repurchased under the normal course issuer bid in the quarter [MDA2Q26 page:26 "we did not repurchase or cancel any shares pursuant to our NCIB"]. Sixth, asset monetization: management says it is in discussions on TELUS Health non-core assets and is advancing the monetization of non-core real estate, with proceeds directed to debt reduction [REL2Q26 page:4 "the company remains active in the market on TELUS Health-related non-core assets"]. Assets, buyers, prices and timing are Not supplied, so no leverage effect can be estimated.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Perimeter and structural subordination. Evidence: the buy-in of the TELUS Digital minority closed October 31, 2025 and Terrion has outside equity with TELUS holding 50.1 per cent [Q3FS page:64 "retained a 50.1% voting and economic interest in Terrion"]; the senior notes are effectively subordinated to obligations of, or guaranteed by, subsidiaries (CP-1). Mechanism: cash generated in Terrion is shared with the outside holder, and any creditors of Terrion (its own debt is Not supplied) would rank ahead of the parent's notes, while TELUS Digital cash flows now fully accrue to the group but carry impairment and demand risk. Implication: a creditor of the parent depends on upstreaming from subsidiaries; guarantor and Terrion terms are Not supplied, so the structural position cannot be completed. The counter-evidence is that the parent issues all identified senior debt and TELUS Communications Inc. and TELUS Health Inc. are wholly owned. 2. Revenue durability and margin. Evidence: mobile network revenue 1,743 against 1,723, fixed data services 1,175 against 1,170, TELUS Digital revenue down to 774 from 827, and ARPU declining at a decelerating rate. Mechanism: growth is subscriber-led with flat unit pricing, so incremental margin depends on cost programs, which management has enlarged (restructuring assumption of approximately $900 million). Implication: free cash flow is exposed to price competition and Digital demand; management lowered 2026 guidance. The counter-evidence is subscriber growth in connected devices and internet. 3. Capital allocation and deleveraging path. Evidence: dividend reset, capital expenditures guidance of approximately $2.6 billion, asset sale processes without terms, and a leverage target moved to year-end 2028. Mechanism: debt reduction depends on lower dividends and unquantified proceeds while capital intensity is higher in 2026 and a spectrum auction follows in October 2027. Implication: leverage tolerance is limited near term; monitor the next release for the capital returns framework and any asset sale agreements. The counter-evidence is the investment-grade wording and covenant headroom reported in CP-1. 4. Regulatory risk to revenue durability. Evidence: the wholesale fibre access framework requires aggregated access to TELUS fibre networks and is under appeal, with hearings likely late 2026 or early 2027 [MDA2Q26 page:67 "The appeal and judicial review will be heard together, likely in late 2026 or early 2027"]. Mechanism (analyst interpretation): wholesale access can reduce retail fibre share and price. Implication: outcome is uncertain and unquantified in the pinned sources; the issuer does not state a financial effect.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: TELUS Corporation is a large Canadian telecommunications borrower whose credit is sound on liquidity and covenants today but weakening in direction. The strongest support is scale and recurring mobile and fibre earnings (LTM Adjusted EBITDA C$ 7,315 million), a reported leverage ratio of 3.5x against a 4.25x covenant, cash of C$ 1,387 million, C$ 657 million of revolver availability to 2030 and investment-grade rating wording. The weakest point is leverage: reported 3.5x relies on half equity credit for C$ 7,322 million of junior subordinated notes, gross debt to EBITDA is 4.30x, cash interest cover fell to 4.62x and 2026 guidance was cut. What decides the outcome is whether the dividend reset, capital discipline and unquantified asset sales bring leverage toward the year-end 2028 target while commercial paper and bond markets remain open.

citations.quote: TELUS Corporation is a large Canadian telecommunications borrower whose credit is sound on liquidity and covenants today but weakening in direction. The weakest point is leverage: reported 3.5x relies on half equity credit for C$ 7,322 million of junior subordinated notes, gross debt to EBITDA is 4.30x, cash interest cover fell to 4.62x and 2026 guidance was cut. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, leverage is the central issue and depends on definition. Net debt of C$ 25,963 million over LTM EBITDA excluding restructuring and other costs of C$ 7,315 million is 3.55x unrounded (3.5x as reported), above the issuer's new 2.5x to 3.0x objective range, and below the 4.25x covenant limit by 0.70x on the issuer's own measure. The issuer gives one-half equity credit to its junior subordinated notes; gross debt of C$ 31,456 million is 4.30x LTM EBITDA, and before the equity credit net debt was 4.02x at March 31, 2026. The covenant definitions are not supplied, so headroom is indicative [CP-1: Chart data leverage; Definitions review].

facts.text: Refinancing dependence (Analyst Interpretation). Commercial paper itself depends on rollover, while other near-term maturities can draw on cash, securitization and bank facility availability or new issuance. Market closure would tighten liquidity quickly [CP-1: Chart data liquidity].

## Request
- Issuer: TELUS CORP (issuer id `tu`; registrant name in the filings "TELUS Corporation"; NYSE ticker TU; Commission File Number 001-15144), as of 2026-11-05, information cutoff 2026-11-05 (context).

- Run: `tu-2026-11-05-credit_snapshot-host`, pathway `credit_snapshot`, case kind public. Requested downstream modules: CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 (the launcher's `minimum` set). CP-0 runs first as their dependency.

- Context settings (not issuer evidence): reporting currency CAD, current period `q2-2026`, prior period `fy-2025`. The context leaves borrower, parent, guarantor, rating, quote, valuation and deal-term fields blank. A blank is not evidence of absence.
- Execution: host session. The host read the pinned files and wrote this answer. No provider was called.
- Question: can the supplied public filings support CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5, and what remains blocked?

- Assertion: SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED. No credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion is given. No figure is normalized, reconciled or calculated here.

- Currency and units: the sources report in Canadian dollars, in millions unless stated. MD&A page:8: "All currency amounts are stated in Canadian dollars, unless otherwise specified". This matches the context. Some debt is U.S. dollar denominated and is stated as such in the notes.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The supplied TELUS filings support all four downstream analyses with stated limits. The latest quarter is well covered, but audited annual statements, second-quarter notes and the debt agreements are absent. | Medium | Audited 2025 statements and second-quarter 2026 notes are not supplied, so annual and debt-by-series figures rest on later filings and quarterly summaries. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The annual report filing is only a cover document. The audited annual statements and the annual information form are listed as exhibits but are not supplied. | Full-year 2025 figures must be assembled from quarterly sources, which weakens annual comparisons. | High |

| The second-quarter management discussion and results release give liquidity, covenant, facility and debt-movement figures at the latest quarter-end. | Liquidity and covenant headroom can be assessed at June 30, 2026 from located figures. | High |

| The second-quarter interim statement notes are not supplied. The last debt-by-series table and maturity schedule are at March 31, 2026. | Debt composition and the refinancing schedule at June 30, 2026 cannot be verified series by series. | High |

| Segment reporting was restated from 2026, and the latest quarter brought a dividend reset, revised guidance, an impairment and management changes. | Earlier segment figures and guidance are not like-for-like; later work must label periods and vintages. | Medium |
| Credit agreements, indentures and named rating-agency ratings are not supplied. | Covenant definitions, guarantees and rating-trigger terms rest on issuer summaries only. | High |
### Readiness view

The effective source set can support all four selected consumers, each with limitations. No consumer is conditional or blocked, because every consumer has located statements, notes or narrative for the latest quarter and for several earlier periods. The strongest limits are three missing documents. First, the audited fiscal year 2025 financial statements and annual MD&A (Exhibit 99.4 to the Form 40-F) and the annual information form (Exhibit 99.3) are named in the exhibit index but are not in the pack. Second, the June 30, 2026 interim financial statements and notes are not in the pack; only the MD&A and the results release for that quarter are. Third, the indentures, credit agreements and securitization agreement are not in the pack. These limits are carried into each consumer assessment below. This is a statement of source sufficiency only. It does not say that any downstream analysis is complete or that any figure has been checked.

- Management change: page:3 "Gopi Chande, Chief Financial Officer". The May 8, 2026 release quotes "Doug French, Executive Vice-president and CFO" (page:4), so the CFO named differs between the two releases. The February release announces the CEO change (page:13).
- Cross-reference: page:5 "See Note 18(b) of the interim consolidated financial statements for additional details". Those interim statements are not in the pack.
#### MD&A, second quarter 2026 (`6-K-EX-99.2_2026-06-30_tu-20260630xex99d2.htm.jsonl`)

- Family and authority: management's discussion and analysis furnished as Exhibit 99.2. Page:9: "This MD&A and the interim consolidated financial statements were reviewed by our Audit Committee and authorized by our Board of Directors (Board) for issuance on July 31, 2026". Unaudited. It is management commentary with statement-derived tables, not the financial statements themselves.

- Located content: section 6 changes in financial position (page:50 and page:51, including "Current maturities of long-term debt" and "Long-term debt" at June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025); section 7 liquidity (cash flows page:51, financing page:55 to page:56, measures page:59); credit facilities (page:60 "At June 30, 2026, we had $657 million of liquidity available from the TELUS revolving credit facility"); covenants (page:61 "As at June 30, 2026, our consolidated leverage ratio was 3.5 to 1.00 and our consolidated coverage ratio was 4.9 to 1.00"); short-term borrowings (page:62 "Available liquidity under this agreement was $680 million as at June 30, 2026" and a separate "$344 million" non-revolving facility); total liquidity wording (page:63 "we had over $2.7 billion of liquidity available at June 30, 2026"); credit ratings (page:62 "We continued to have investment-grade ratings in the second quarter of 2026 and as at July 31, 2026"); eight-quarter income table (section 5.2, page:29 and following).

- Debt movements: page:56 commercial paper "a balance of $2.1 billion (US$1.5 billion) at June 30, 2026"; page:56 "Subsequent to June 30, 2026, the remaining $300 million was paid upon maturity in the normal course"; page:50 reclassification of a U.S. dollar note series to current.

- Limits: it points to Notes 18, 22, 26, 29 and 31 of interim statements not supplied (for example page:50 "See Note 22 of the interim consolidated financial statements"). It incorporates the 2025 annual MD&A by reference, which is not supplied.

### Version relationships and conflicts

- Guidance vintages. The May 8, 2026 release states free cash flow of approximately $2.45 billion and leverage targets for year-end 2026 and year-end 2027 (page:1). The July 31, 2026 release states "full-year free cash flow is anticipated to be approximately $1.8 billion" (page:2) and says "The company had previously targeted net debt to Adjusted EBITDA of approximately 3.0-times or lower by year-end 2027" (page:4). The later release controls current guidance. Both are retained as dated management claims. This is a superseded claim, not a document conflict.

- Metric naming. The July release says "Net debt to Adjusted EBITDA of 3.5-times" (page:2). The MD&A reports the covenant-related measure "Net debt to EBITDA – excluding restructuring and other costs" at 3.5 times (page:59). The names differ and the MD&A defines its measure in section 11.1. CP-1 must state which definition it uses and must not treat the two as the same measure without reading the definitions.

- Covenant wording. The March 31, 2026 statements describe the second covenant as an "operating cash flow to interest expense ratio" (page:43). The MD&A calls it the "consolidated coverage ratio" and states 4.9 (page:61), and also reports a separate "EBITDA – excluding restructuring and other costs interest coverage" measure (page:59). The MD&A says "There are certain minor differences in the calculation of the leverage ratio and coverage ratio under the revolving credit facility" (page:61). The facility definitions are not supplied, so the exact covenant calculation cannot be verified.

- Segment structure. The February 12, 2026 release and the September 30, 2025 statements use the earlier structure. The 2026 filings restate it retrospectively for the TELUS Digital privatization (MD&A page:9; May release page:1). Comparing segment figures across these vintages needs a label for each source.

- Perimeter. TELUS Digital was consolidated with a non-controlling interest until the transaction closed on October 31, 2025 (September statements page:64; March statements page:48). Terrion has had a non-controlling interest since July 2025 (September statements page:64). Period comparisons across these dates are not like-for-like.

- Duplicates. The quarterly figures in the July release repeat figures in the MD&A. The MD&A is the more detailed source for the quarter; neither is independent corroboration of the other. Dividend reset statements recur in the July release and the MD&A.
- No hash duplicates are present among the seven sources.
### Identity and perimeter

- Reporting entity and debt issuer: TELUS Corporation. The long-term debt note presents "TELUS Corporation senior notes", "TELUS Corporation commercial paper" and "TELUS Corporation junior subordinated notes" (March statements page:39).

- Principal subsidiaries named: TELUS Communications Inc. and TELUS Health Inc. (March statements page:4, "Our principal subsidiaries"). The TELUS Digital segment sat in TELUS International (Cda) Inc. until October 31, 2025.

- Structural ranking. The notes are described as "effectively subordinated to all existing and future obligations of, or guaranteed by, our subsidiaries" (March statements page:39 and page:45). Whether any subsidiary guarantees a TELUS Corporation instrument is not stated in the supplied text. That is a gap, not a finding of no guarantees.
- Junior subordinated notes receive partial equity credit in leverage ratios: MD&A page:57 "only one-half of the principal of our junior subordinated notes is included as debt".
- Roles not resolved by the sources: restricted and unrestricted group boundaries, covenant borrower group and guarantor list. The context leaves these blank.
### Information-availability boundary
- Latest-dated source: the July 31, 2026 release and MD&A. The as-of date and cutoff are November 5, 2026, so the supplied set ends about three months before the as-of date.

- Nothing dated after July 31, 2026 is supplied. The July release says the fuller capital-returns framework follows with third-quarter 2026 results "in November" (page:3). Those results are Not supplied; whether they were published before the cutoff cannot be determined from the pack.

- Subsequent events inside the pack are bounded to the MD&A and release dates: the remaining $300 million of the 2.75% Series CZ notes paid at maturity after June 30, 2026 (MD&A page:56); the dividend payable on October 1, 2026 and the removal of the dividend reinvestment discount effective October 1, 2026 (release page:4). Both are labelled as dated before or at the release and do not show later outcomes.

### Analytical read-through

- Usable coverage: three interim sources (September 30, 2025 statements; March 31, 2026 statements; June 30, 2026 MD&A) plus the fourth quarter 2025 and 2026 releases give a continuous quarterly record. The December 31, 2025 statement of financial position is available as a comparative in the March 2026 statements (page:1 and page:2) and the MD&A (page:50 and page:51). The MD&A eight-quarter table covers each quarter of 2025 and 2026.

- Strongest contrary evidence: the audited annual layer is missing, and the latest quarter contains events that change the credit picture. The July release reports a net loss driven by an impairment relating to TELUS Digital and a dividend reset to support deleveraging. Management also states the leverage target date moved to year-end 2028. These are management claims in a release, and the MD&A is the filed document that carries the figures.

- Source risk mechanism, evidence to risk to consequence. First, evidence: the Form 40-F text incorporates its financial statements by reference from an exhibit not in the pack. Risk: an analyst could mistake the cover document for the annual report and treat full-year 2025 figures as audited. Consequence: CP-1 must label fiscal year 2025 as assembled from quarterly sources, and CP-5 must not treat quarterly sums as audited. Second, evidence: debt by series, maturities and the facility table are in the March 2026 notes, while the June 2026 MD&A gives only movements and totals. Risk: the refinancing schedule and series list are one quarter old, and the quarter had redemptions, a note reclassified to current and growth in commercial paper. Consequence: CP-2 can state liquidity at June 30, 2026 but must date the maturity schedule at March 31, 2026. Third, evidence: junior subordinated notes get partial equity credit in the leverage measure, and covenant definitions are not supplied. Risk: reported leverage and covenant leverage may differ from a gross-debt view. Consequence: CP-1 and CP-2 must show each definition and carry the gap instead of assuming headroom from the reported ratio.

- What cannot proceed: verification of covenant calculations against agreement definitions; guarantor-level or restricted-group analysis; a series-by-series debt schedule at June 30, 2026; audited full-year 2025 tie-outs; any event after July 31, 2026.

- Next evidence action: supply Exhibit 99.4 and Exhibit 99.3 of the Form 40-F, the Exhibit 99.1 interim statements that accompany the June 30, 2026 MD&A, the credit agreements and indentures, a rating-agency source, and any filing between July 31, 2026 and November 5, 2026.

No new calculation. CP-0 does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. Figures quoted above are copied from the sources with their locators. No sum, ratio or difference is computed in this handoff.

### Financial base view

TELUS is a large, investment-grade-rated Canadian telecommunications issuer whose reported leverage is 3.5 times net debt to EBITDA excluding restructuring and other costs at June 30, 2026, above both its previous and its newly set objective ranges, but below the covenant limit of 4.25 times. The financial base can be built from the pinned sources for the latest quarter and for four consecutive balance sheet dates, with limits. Reported leverage depends on a definition that gives half equity credit to the junior subordinated notes and adjusts for hedging items, so a gross view is also shown: total debt, including lease liabilities and short-term borrowings, is 4.30 times LTM EBITDA excluding restructuring and other costs. Cash interest cover on the same EBITDA is 4.62 times, down from 5.09 times a quarter earlier, partly because cash interest paid in Q2 2026 included a prepayment premium. Liquidity at June 30, 2026 is cash and temporary investments of 1,387, revolver availability of 657 after a 2,093 commercial paper backstop, securitization availability of 680 and a further 344 on a non-revolving bank facility due June 2027. Current maturities of long-term debt are 3,802. The second quarter brought a 2,135 impairment relating to TELUS Digital, a net loss of 1,830, a dividend reset and lower guidance. The view is restricted by missing audited FY2025 statements, missing second-quarter notes and missing agreements, so FY2025 flows are assembled from quarters and the debt register is dated March 31, 2026. ### Definitions review

- EBITDA is operating revenues and other income less goods and services purchased and employee benefits expense [MDA2Q26 page:81 "EBITDA as calculated by TELUS is equivalent to Operating revenues and other income less the total of Goods and services purchased expense and Employee benefits expense"]. It includes restructuring and other costs; impairment is added back in the segment reconciliation, so EBITDA is stated before impairment [REL2Q26 page:20].

- EBITDA excluding restructuring and other costs is the leverage and coverage numerator. In Q2 2026 and every quarter in the eight-quarter table it equals Adjusted EBITDA [REL2Q26 page:20 "EBITDA – excluding restructuring and other costs and Adjusted EBITDA 1,639"]. Adjusted EBITDA excludes items the issuer considers unusual [MDA2Q26 page:81].

- Net debt is long-term debt less the junior subordinated notes equity credit, plus debt issuance costs, less hedging derivative and accumulated other comprehensive income items, less cash, plus short-term borrowings [Q1FS page:7 "TELUS Corporation junior subordinated notes equity credit deducted in calculating net debt"]. For the equity credit, "only one-half of the principal of our junior subordinated notes is included as debt" [MDA2Q26 page:57]. The net debt components at June 30, 2026 are not printed in the pinned sources because they sit in the unsupplied Note 3.

- Net interest cost is financing costs adjusted for pension net interest, capitalized interest, debt-purchase gains and virtual power purchase agreement items [MDA2Q26 page:85]. It is an accrual measure, not cash interest.

- Covenants: leverage must not exceed 4.25 to 1.00 and coverage must not be less than 2.00 to 1.00 at each quarter-end; the reported ratios at June 30, 2026 are 3.5 and 4.9, and "There are certain minor differences in the calculation" against the management measures [MDA2Q26 page:61]. The Q1FS describes the second test as an operating cash flow to interest expense ratio [Q1FS page:43 "our operating cash flow to interest expense ratio must not be less than 2.00:1.00"]. The credit agreement definitions are not supplied.

- Objective range changed. In Q1FS the objective range is 2.2 to 2.7 times [Q1FS page:8 "Our long-term objective range for this ratio is 2.2 – 2.7 times"]. The June 2026 MD&A shows 2.5 to 3.0 times, with an objective of about 3.0 times in 2028 [MDA2Q26 page:27 "Net debt to EBITDA – excluding restructuring and other costs ratio of 2.5 to 3.0 times"]. Comparisons to the objective must name the vintage.

- Free cash flow is the issuer's non-GAAP measure and excludes certain working capital changes, proceeds from divested assets and other items [MDA2Q26 page:83 "Free cash flow: We report this measure"]. It is not a covenant measure.

### Interpretation: evidence, mechanism, implication

- Leverage is definition-dependent. Evidence: net debt of 25,963 uses half equity credit for junior subordinated notes and EBITDA of 7,315. Mechanism: the notes are subordinated and carry a rating-event repurchase at 102 per cent, so the equity credit depends on agency treatment; if lost, reported leverage rises toward the gross figure. Implication: senior creditors should monitor the gross ratio of 4.30 times as well as the covenant ratio, because covenant headroom is 0.70 times on the issuer's own definition.

- Cash interest cover is moving down. Evidence: EBITDA over cash interest paid fell from 5.31 at FY2025 to 4.62 at June 30, 2026. Mechanism: interest paid rose by 142 in Q2 2026 and 201 in H1 2026 on 2025 junior subordinated issuance, the promissory note and the prepayment premium, while LTM EBITDA excluding restructuring and other costs fell from 7,354 to 7,315. Implication: cash cover has less margin, although part of the Q2 2026 rise is one-off.

- Refinancing and liquidity. Evidence: current maturities of long-term debt of 3,802, commercial paper of 2.1 billion fully backstopped by a revolver with 657 availability. Mechanism: commercial paper is classified as current but is supported by the revolver, so it consumes revolver capacity one for one and the availability of 657 is what remains after that backstop. The other current maturities, including the US$600 million 2.80% notes reclassified to current and the Series CZ balance paid in July 2026, rely on cash of 1,387, securitization availability of 680, non-revolving availability of 344 or new issuance. Implication: near-term maturities depend on commercial paper rollover and market access; the investment-grade wording supports access but ratings are not supplied and not tested here.

- Earnings quality. Evidence: Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of 1,777 versus 1,812 and a 2,135 non-cash impairment; Digital Adjusted EBITDA 72 versus 89. Mechanism: the impairment does not affect EBITDA or covenants, which are not impacted by revaluation of goodwill [MDA2Q26 page:61 "The covenants are not impacted by revaluation"], but signals lower recoverable value in the TELUS Digital unit. Implication: covenant headroom is unaffected by the impairment, while the lower guidance affects forward leverage.

- Dividend reset. Evidence: dividends paid 864 in H1 2026 against free cash flow of 1,128 in the same half. Mechanism: the quarterly dividend falls from 0.4184 to 0.1875 per share. Implication: management cites this as a deleveraging lever; the 2.7 billion saving through 2028 is a management estimate.

CP-2 should carry the definition dependence of leverage (3.5 reported, 4.30 gross), the covenant headroom of 0.70 times on the management measure, the March 31, 2026 date of the debt register and maturity wall, the securitization and non-revolving sources that sit outside the revolver, and the missing agreements and ratings. CP-5 should treat FY2025 figures as assembled, not audited.

## Findings
### Reader summary

The creditor-relevant change is a buy-in of TELUS Digital minorities, tower equity sold at Terrion, a dividend reset and weaker guidance; no sponsor is identified. | Medium | The annual information form, deal documents and later events are not supplied, so ownership detail and asset-sale terms cannot be confirmed. |

| Management reset the dividend, lowered 2026 guidance and moved the leverage target date to year-end 2028. | Cash retained for debt reduction rises, but the date and objective range have been moved twice in six months. | Medium |

### Business and transaction view

TELUS Corporation is a British Columbia company and one of Canada's largest telecommunications groups, with three reporting segments: TELUS technology solutions (mobile, fixed data and voice, security and automation, agriculture and consumer goods technology), TELUS Health (employee and family assistance programs, benefits administration, virtual care) and TELUS Digital (digital solutions, AI and data, trust and safety, customer experience management). The sources describe no controlling shareholder, no sponsor and no pending change of control; ownership detail beyond the share count and a Canadian-ownership voting restriction is not supplied. The creditor-relevant structure is a parent that issues all identified senior notes, commercial paper and junior subordinated notes and is effectively subordinated to obligations of, or guaranteed by, its subsidiaries, with a subsidiary (Terrion) holding minority outside equity. The relevant history is a 2025 reshaping of the perimeter: the acquisition of Workplace Options in May 2025, the establishment of Terrion in July 2025 with outside equity, and the buy-in of the TELUS Digital minority on October 31, 2025, followed in 2026 by a 2,135 impairment of TELUS Digital, a management transition, a dividend reset, lower guidance and asset sale processes. Business risk is anchored by a large mobile and fibre base with declining ARPU at a decelerating rate, partly offset by growth in connected devices and internet connections. As an analyst reading, TELUS Digital depends on external clients and intersegment work, and Health earnings were built partly by acquisition. The view is restricted by the absence of the annual information form, the transaction agreements and any filing after July 31, 2026.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

TELUS is not the subject of a sponsor buyout, merger or refinancing in the pinned sources, so no deal-level use of proceeds, sponsor or closing condition applies; one Insufficient Information row stands for any transaction after July 31, 2026, which is Not supplied. The completed transactions that shape the creditor's perimeter are these. First, the TELUS Digital privatization: on June 12, 2025 TELUS Corporation submitted a non-binding indication of interest to the board of TELUS International (Cda) Inc. [Q3FS page:63 "submitted a non-binding indication of interest"], signed a definitive agreement on September 2, 2025 at "for a price per share of US$4.50" [Q3FS page:64 "for a price per share of US$4.50"], payable in cash, Common Shares or a combination subject to a 25 per cent cap on shares, and closed on October 31, 2025 [Q3FS page:64 "The transaction closed October 31, 2025"]. The final cash and share mix and the cash outlay are Not supplied in the pinned sources. Second, Terrion: a wireless tower infrastructure partnership established on July 24, 2025 that issued equity to an outside holder for net cash proceeds of 1,246 [Q3FS page:65 "Net cash proceeds $ 1,261"], after which TELUS keeps 50.1 per cent voting and economic interest and holds a call option exercisable in whole in September 2027 if there is a partner dispute or after September 2057 at generally the greater of fair value and a multiple on invested capital [Q3FS page:64 "call option"]. The outside holder is not named in the pinned sources. The Terrion non-controlling interest was 792 at September 30, 2025 and non-controlling interests were 808 at June 30, 2026 (CP-1). Third, Workplace Options: TELUS acquired 100 per cent on May 1, 2025 [Q3FS page:44 "On May 1, 2025, we acquired 100% of Workplace Options"], with cash consideration of 453 funded in part by 280 (US$200 million) of preferred shares issued by a subsidiary to a private equity investor; the preferred shares were later exchanged for a US$200 million promissory note and the note was repaid in Q2 2026 with a prepayment premium of 51 (CP-1). Fourth, liability management: tender offers in June and December 2025 that bought back senior notes (series CL, CU, CW, CAB, CAE and U.S. dollar notes), with gains on purchase of long-term debt of 222 in Q3 2025 and 81 in Q4 2025 [MDA2Q26 page:29 "Gain on purchase of long-term debt"], the full redemption of the 3.75% Series CV notes on January 16, 2026, the redemption of 500 of the 2.75% Series CZ notes on May 8, 2026, and the payment of the remaining 300 of that series at maturity after June 30, 2026 (CP-1). Fifth, equity and distributions: the dividend reset announced July 31, 2026 and the end of the dividend reinvestment plan discount effective October 1, 2026 [REL2Q26 page:4 "representing a reset of 55 per cent to an annualized amount of $0.75 per share"]; no shares were repurchased under the normal course issuer bid in the quarter [MDA2Q26 page:26 "we did not repurchase or cancel any shares pursuant to our NCIB"]. Sixth, asset monetization: management says it is in discussions on TELUS Health non-core assets and is advancing the monetization of non-core real estate, with proceeds directed to debt reduction [REL2Q26 page:4 "the company remains active in the market on TELUS Health-related non-core assets"]. Assets, buyers, prices and timing are Not supplied, so no leverage effect can be estimated.

New debt issues in the pinned sources, as printed in the March 31, 2026 debt note (all unsecured and issued by TELUS Corporation unless stated): fixed-to-fixed rate junior subordinated notes issued in 2025 and December 2025 comprising Series CAR 6.25 per cent (1,500 outstanding, due July 2055), Series CAS 6.75 per cent (925, due July 2055), U.S. dollar Series A 6.625 per cent (US$700 million, due October 2055), Series B 7.000 per cent (US$800 million, due October 2055), Series C 6.375 per cent (US$800 million, due June 2056), Series D 6.625 per cent (US$700 million, due June 2056), Series CAT 5.375 per cent (400, due June 2056) and Series CAU 5.875 per cent (400, due June 2056) [Q1FS page:45 "Series CAT"]. The Series C, D, CAT and CAU notes were issued in December 2025. The junior subordinated notes are subordinated to all senior indebtedness, receive one-half equity credit in leverage ratios in the initial post-issuance decade, and carry a repurchase offer at 102 per cent upon a rating event (CP-1). No new senior note series issued in the first half of 2026 is itemized in the pinned sources; long-term debt issued in that half is described in the MD&A mainly as commercial paper activity with a commercial paper balance of $2.1 billion (US$1.5 billion) at June 30, 2026 [MDA2Q26 page:56 "a balance of $2.1 billion (US$1.5 billion) at June 30, 2026"]. Sustainability-linked note series (CAF, CAG, CAJ, CAK, CAN and the 3.40 per cent U.S. dollar series) were issued before 2025 and the debt table refers to trigger events and step-ups for them (CP-1 debt register).
### Ownership and control

- Controlling shareholder or sponsor: Not supplied and none indicated. Category: Insufficient Information for any holder above a threshold. The issuer is a listed company with a Canadian-ownership restriction on voting [Q1FS page:47 "no less than 66-2/3%"].

- Subsidiary equity: Terrion has outside equity and a call option held by TELUS (above). The outside holder's rights over distributions, governance and exit are Not supplied beyond the call option, so the claim ranking between Terrion's creditors, the outside holder and TELUS Corporation cannot be set.
- Prior ownership: until October 31, 2025 TELUS Digital had public minority holders and a non-controlling interest of 1,649 at September 30, 2025 in TELUS Corporation's consolidated equity (CP-1).

- Dividend recapitalization history: none documented. Capacity to distribute: the indentures limit security on indebtedness, sale-leaseback transactions and new indebtedness by TELUS and certain subsidiaries, and do not restrict dividends in the text supplied [Q1FS page:39 "The notes’ indentures contain covenants"]. The full covenant package is Not supplied.

### Capital allocation and disclosure

Mechanism: lower cash dividends (864 paid in H1 2026 per CP-1) increase cash available for debt repayment; the issuer states approximately $2.7 billion in cumulative cash savings through 2028 directed to deleveraging (management estimate).

- Capital expenditures and spectrum: capital expenditures guidance raised; spectrum payments of 373 in the first six months of 2026 and an auction in October 2027 are cash calls that can delay deleveraging. Mechanism: spectrum is financed with debt and cash; the issuer says spectrum acquisitions increased the leverage ratio by approximately 0.6 and the junior subordinated notes equity credit decreased it by 0.5 [MDA2Q26 page:59 "the acquisition of spectrum licences increased the ratio by approximately 0.6"].
- Acquisitions and disposals: Workplace Options (cash 453) in 2025; asset monetization under way in 2026. Appetite for further acquisitions is not inferred from one deal.
- Disclosure for monitoring: the debt schedule and maturity schedule are dated March 31, 2026; covenant certificates, credit agreements and an add-back bridge are Not supplied (severity Medium).

The fall of 10.7 million between the last two quarter-ends has no explanation in the pinned sources. Treat the counts as management operating indicators, not trendable |

Later source controls current policy; earlier ranges are history |

| Free cash flow guidance | [REL1Q26 page:1 "Consolidated Free Cash Flow of approximately $2.45 billion"] | [REL2Q26 page:2 "full-year free cash flow is anticipated to be approximately $1.8 billion"] | Superseded guidance, not a document conflict |
### Credit translations

1. Perimeter and structural subordination. Evidence: the buy-in of the TELUS Digital minority closed October 31, 2025 and Terrion has outside equity with TELUS holding 50.1 per cent [Q3FS page:64 "retained a 50.1% voting and economic interest in Terrion"]; the senior notes are effectively subordinated to obligations of, or guaranteed by, subsidiaries (CP-1). Mechanism: cash generated in Terrion is shared with the outside holder, and any creditors of Terrion (its own debt is Not supplied) would rank ahead of the parent's notes, while TELUS Digital cash flows now fully accrue to the group but carry impairment and demand risk. Implication: a creditor of the parent depends on upstreaming from subsidiaries; guarantor and Terrion terms are Not supplied, so the structural position cannot be completed. The counter-evidence is that the parent issues all identified senior debt and TELUS Communications Inc. and TELUS Health Inc. are wholly owned.

2. Revenue durability and margin. Evidence: mobile network revenue 1,743 against 1,723, fixed data services 1,175 against 1,170, TELUS Digital revenue down to 774 from 827, and ARPU declining at a decelerating rate. Mechanism: growth is subscriber-led with flat unit pricing, so incremental margin depends on cost programs, which management has enlarged (restructuring assumption of approximately $900 million). Implication: free cash flow is exposed to price competition and Digital demand; management lowered 2026 guidance. The counter-evidence is subscriber growth in connected devices and internet.

3. Capital allocation and deleveraging path. Evidence: dividend reset, capital expenditures guidance of approximately $2.6 billion, asset sale processes without terms, and a leverage target moved to year-end 2028. Mechanism: debt reduction depends on lower dividends and unquantified proceeds while capital intensity is higher in 2026 and a spectrum auction follows in October 2027. Implication: leverage tolerance is limited near term; monitor the next release for the capital returns framework and any asset sale agreements. The counter-evidence is the investment-grade wording and covenant headroom reported in CP-1.

4. Regulatory risk to revenue durability. Evidence: the wholesale fibre access framework requires aggregated access to TELUS fibre networks and is under appeal, with hearings likely late 2026 or early 2027 [MDA2Q26 page:67 "The appeal and judicial review will be heard together, likely in late 2026 or early 2027"]. Mechanism (analyst interpretation): wholesale access can reduce retail fibre share and price. Implication: outcome is uncertain and unquantified in the pinned sources; the issuer does not state a financial effect.
### Consumers

## Calculations

No new calculation. Figures repeated from CP-1 or a source are copied unchanged: Terrion net cash proceeds 1,246 are the printed net figure from the Terrion equity table (1,261 issue less 15 other). The change in healthcare lives covered between quarter-ends is a difference of the two printed values: 169.6 less 158.9 = 10.7 million. The dividend cut of 55 per cent and the annualized 0.75 and 1.6736 are copied from the release.
## Gaps

## Next module

CP-2 (fundamental credit synthesis) is next, then CP-5. CP-2 should combine this handoff's perimeter, Terrion, capital allocation and conflict rows with the CP-1 definition dependence of leverage, the March 31, 2026 date of the debt register, and the missing agreements. ## Request

This is the fundamental credit synthesis for TELUS CORP (issuer id `tu`), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit_snapshot pathway, written from the financial base and business context handoffs only. It covers business risk, financial risk, liquidity and the gaps that limit them, with no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources

CP-2 reads no source text. Every figure and fact below comes from the two upstream handoffs, which in turn rest on the seven issuer sources listed here. Amounts are Canadian dollars (C$) in millions unless stated, as in the handoffs.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| TELUS has solid liquidity and covenant headroom, but leverage is above its own objective and depends on equity credit, cash interest cover is falling and guidance has been cut. The credit is under pressure. | Medium | Audited 2025 statements, deal and financing agreements, named ratings and anything after July 31, 2026 are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Reported net debt to EBITDA is 3.5x against a 4.25x covenant, but gross debt to EBITDA is 4.30x because junior subordinated notes get half equity credit. | Covenant headroom of 0.70x holds on the issuer's own definition; a gross view shows less cushion. | Medium |
| Cash interest cover fell to 4.62x at June 30, 2026 from 5.31x at FY2025. | Less earnings cushion over cash interest while leverage is still above objective. | Medium |

| Cash, revolver, securitization and bank facility availability are large, but current debt maturities of C$ 3,802 million include commercial paper supported by the revolver. | Near-term maturities depend on commercial paper rollover and market access rather than committed term funding. | Medium |

| Guidance was cut, TELUS Digital was impaired by C$ 2,135 million and the leverage target moved to year-end 2028. | Deleveraging now depends on the dividend reset and asset sales whose terms are not supplied. | Medium |

| The Terrion minority equity, the TELUS Digital buy-in and unknown guarantee terms shape structural position. | The parent's creditors rank behind subsidiary obligations; the exact structure cannot be completed. | Low |
### Credit view

TELUS Corporation is a large Canadian telecommunications borrower whose credit is sound on liquidity and covenants today but weakening in direction. The strongest support is scale and recurring mobile and fibre earnings (LTM Adjusted EBITDA C$ 7,315 million), a reported leverage ratio of 3.5x against a 4.25x covenant, cash of C$ 1,387 million, C$ 657 million of revolver availability to 2030 and investment-grade rating wording. The weakest point is leverage: reported 3.5x relies on half equity credit for C$ 7,322 million of junior subordinated notes, gross debt to EBITDA is 4.30x, cash interest cover fell to 4.62x and 2026 guidance was cut. What decides the outcome is whether the dividend reset, capital discipline and unquantified asset sales bring leverage toward the year-end 2028 target while commercial paper and bond markets remain open.
### Key findings

First, leverage is the central issue and depends on definition. Net debt of C$ 25,963 million over LTM EBITDA excluding restructuring and other costs of C$ 7,315 million is 3.55x unrounded (3.5x as reported), above the issuer's new 2.5x to 3.0x objective range, and below the 4.25x covenant limit by 0.70x on the issuer's own measure. The issuer gives one-half equity credit to its junior subordinated notes; gross debt of C$ 31,456 million is 4.30x LTM EBITDA, and before the equity credit net debt was 4.02x at March 31, 2026. The covenant definitions are not supplied, so headroom is indicative [CP-1: Chart data leverage; Definitions review].

Second, cash interest cover is declining. LTM EBITDA over cash interest paid was 4.62x at June 30, 2026, 5.09x at March 31, 2026 and 5.31x at FY2025. Interest paid rose on 2025 junior subordinated issuance, a promissory note and a C$ 51 million prepayment premium, so part of the fall is one-off; the issuer's own coverage measure is 4.9x against a 2.00x covenant floor [CP-1: Chart data interest cover].

Third, liquidity is adequate; refinancing relies on market access. Cash is C$ 1,387 million, revolver availability C$ 657 million after a C$ 2,093 million commercial paper backstop, securitization availability C$ 680 million and a non-revolving facility C$ 344 million. Current maturities of long-term debt are C$ 3,802 million and include commercial paper that the revolver supports. The maturity schedule, dated March 31, 2026, shows C$ 3,148 million falling due in the rest of 2026, C$ 1,928 million in 2027 and C$ 2,319 million in 2028 [CP-1: Chart data liquidity and debt maturities].

Fourth, earnings and guidance weakened in the quarter. Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was C$ 1,777 million against C$ 1,812 million, with a net loss of C$ 1,830 million after a C$ 2,135 million non-cash TELUS Digital impairment, which does not touch covenants. Management lowered 2026 guidance: service revenue flat to a 2 per cent decline, Adjusted EBITDA down 2 to 4 per cent, free cash flow about C$ 1.8 billion from about C$ 2.45 billion, and capital expenditures about C$ 2.6 billion from about C$ 2.3 billion (Management Language) [CP-1: Subsequent events and guidance].

Fifth, the deleveraging plan rests on management actions rather than organic cash flow. The quarterly dividend was reset to C$ 0.1875 per share from C$ 0.4184, with management estimating about C$ 2.7 billion of cash savings through 2028; the 3.0x target date moved from year-end 2027 to year-end 2028 and the objective range moved from 2.2x to 2.7x to 2.5x to 3.0x. Asset sales of TELUS Health non-core assets and real estate are under way with no assets, prices or timing supplied [CP-1A: Capital allocation; Conflicts].

Sixth, the perimeter changed in 2025 and structural position is incomplete. TELUS bought out the TELUS Digital minority on October 31, 2025 and sold minority equity in the Terrion tower partnership for net cash proceeds of C$ 1,246 million while keeping 50.1 per cent. The senior notes are effectively subordinated to subsidiary obligations; guarantor terms and Terrion governance are not supplied [CP-1A: Transaction summary; Ownership and control].
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths.

Scale and recurring earnings (Documentary Fact). TELUS Corporation earned LTM Adjusted EBITDA of C$ 7,315 million, and mobile network revenue of C$ 1,743 million in Q2 2026 compared with C$ 1,723 million a year earlier. Subscriber growth in mobile, connected devices and internet supports revenue visibility even with declining ARPU. This lowers the probability that operating earnings alone force a default; the weakness is pricing, not volume [CP-1: Financials and credit metrics; CP-1A: Company and operating model].

Covenant headroom (Analyst Interpretation on documentary figures). Reported leverage of 3.5x sits 0.70x below the 4.25x limit, an EBITDA cushion of C$ 1,206 million (16.5 per cent) at constant net debt, and coverage of 4.9x sits 2.9x above the 2.00x floor. The covenants are not affected by goodwill revaluation, so the C$ 2,135 million impairment does not reduce headroom. This limits near-term acceleration risk, subject to unseen covenant definitions [CP-1: Covenant and liquidity position].

Liquidity and access (Documentary Fact and Management Language). Cash of C$ 1,387 million, revolver availability of C$ 657 million expiring August 2030, securitization availability of C$ 680 million and a non-revolving facility availability of C$ 344 million cover the issuer's stated objective of at least C$ 1 billion of available liquidity. The investment-grade wording from management supports commercial paper and bond access, though agency ratings are not supplied [CP-1: Covenant and liquidity position].

Management response (Management Language). The dividend reset, removal of the reinvestment plan discount and the end-2028 leverage target direct cash toward debt reduction, and junior subordinated notes and Terrion minority equity have reduced reported leverage. This improves debt service capacity if executed, but the savings figure is a management estimate [CP-1A: Capital allocation and disclosure].
Weaknesses.

Leverage above objective and definition-dependent (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Reported 3.5x exceeds the 2.5x to 3.0x range, gross leverage is 4.30x, and the equity credit on junior subordinated notes depends on agency treatment that is not supplied. If that treatment changed, reported leverage would move toward the gross figure and headroom would shrink [CP-1: Definitions review].

Falling cash interest cover (Documentary Fact). Cover declined from 5.31x to 4.62x over two quarters as interest paid rose, and junior subordinated notes carry coupons of 5.375 to 7.000 per cent. Refinancing of lower-coupon senior notes at current rates would add to interest, an inference the sources do not quantify [CP-1: Chart data interest cover; Debt register].

Weaker earnings momentum and guidance (Management Language and Documentary Fact). Adjusted EBITDA fell, TELUS Digital Adjusted EBITDA was C$ 72 million against C$ 89 million, and management attributes the Digital weakness to demand ramp-downs and churn at certain hyperscale customers. Lower free cash flow guidance reduces internally funded deleveraging and increases reliance on asset sales [CP-1: Segment and KPI view; CP-1A: Company and operating model].

Distributions and capital intensity (Documentary Fact). Dividends declared were 109 per cent of cash from operations less capital expenditures over the twelve months to June 30, 2026, and capital expenditure guidance rose to about C$ 2.6 billion with a spectrum auction in October 2027. The dividend reset addresses the first point after quarter-end; the spectrum payment is a future call on cash [CP-1A: Governance and behaviour; Capital allocation].

Refinancing dependence (Analyst Interpretation). Current maturities of C$ 3,802 million include commercial paper of about C$ 2.1 billion (US$ 1.5 billion) that consumes revolver capacity one for one. Commercial paper itself depends on rollover, while other near-term maturities can draw on cash, securitization and bank facility availability or new issuance. Market closure would tighten liquidity quickly [CP-1: Chart data liquidity].

Structure and information (Insufficient Information). Guarantor terms, Terrion governance and its own debt, the audited annual statements and the credit agreements are not supplied. Missing evidence is not an adverse finding, but it prevents a view of loss given default or covenant robustness and keeps confidence at Medium [CP-0; CP-1A: Gaps].
### Credit thesis

TELUS Corporation is a scale telecommunications borrower with adequate liquidity and covenant headroom whose credit quality is under pressure from above-objective, definition-dependent leverage, falling cash interest cover and lowered guidance, so the outcome depends on delivering dividend-funded deleveraging and asset sales while market access stays open (Analyst Interpretation).
### Credit assessment
- Category: Analyst Interpretation on Documentary Fact figures.

- Confidence: Medium. Not High because the audited annual statements, the financing agreements, named ratings, the Terrion and guarantee terms and every event after July 31, 2026 are not supplied, and because the business context handoff judges this module ready with limitations, not ready.
- Basis: CP-1 financial base (leverage, coverage, liquidity, maturities, guidance) and CP-1A context (perimeter, Terrion, capital allocation, conflicts).

- Inherited limits (restated once): fiscal year 2025 flows are assembled from quarters; the debt register is dated March 31, 2026; segment and perimeter vintages differ; four operating-indicator discrepancies are open.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Deleveraging slips | Lower Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow guidance, higher capital expenditures and unquantified asset sales leave net debt near C$ 25,963 million | Leverage stays above objective and the 2028 target date moves again; monitoring posture tightens | Material |

| Equity credit or covenant definition changes | One-half credit on junior subordinated notes and unseen covenant definitions underpin the reported 3.5x | Reported leverage moves toward the gross 4.30x and headroom narrows | Material |

| Market access and rollover | Commercial paper of about C$ 2.1 billion sits inside current maturities and uses revolver capacity | A market disruption forces use of securitization, bank facilities or cash | Material |
| Cash interest burden | Cash interest cover fell to 4.62x as higher-coupon junior subordinated debt and premiums raised interest paid | Less buffer if EBITDA declines further | Material |
| TELUS Digital further weakness | Client ramp-downs, a C$ 2,135 million impairment and lower Adjusted EBITDA | Pressure on group EBITDA and recoverable values | Material |

| Structural subordination | Notes rank behind subsidiary obligations; Terrion outside equity shares cash flows; guarantees unknown | Loss given default cannot be assessed; upstreaming of cash is assumed | Material |
| Regulatory outcomes | Wholesale fibre access under appeal and spectrum auction in October 2027 | Revenue durability and capital calls; no financial effect stated by the issuer | Minor |
| Information gaps | Missing annual statements, agreements, ratings and post-July 31, 2026 events | Confidence capped at Medium | Minor |
### What would change the view

Monitoring items, not recommendations: an executed asset sale with proceeds applied to debt; third-quarter 2026 results and the capital returns framework promised for November; a change in covenant ratios or the equity credit treatment; commercial paper outstanding relative to revolver availability; whether free cash flow tracks the lowered guidance of about C$ 1.8 billion; and any rating agency action. Each is Not supplied as of the cutoff.
## Calculations

No new calculation. Every figure is restated from the CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs with the same value, unit and period, including 3.5x reported and 3.55x unrounded, 4.30x gross, 4.02x before equity credit at March 31, 2026, 0.70x headroom, the EBITDA cushion of C$ 1,206 million (16.5 per cent), cash interest cover of 4.62x, 5.09x and 5.31x, and the liquidity components.

Consistency with upstream: no figure in the two handoffs is corrected here. The healthcare lives covered, connection count, leverage objective and free cash flow guidance discrepancies logged in the CP-1A handoff are carried as open and are not used as evidence in this synthesis.
## Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters | Affects | Severity | Action |

| Audited FY2025 statements and annual MD&A not supplied; FY2025 flows assembled from quarters | Limits annual comparisons and tie-outs of leverage and cash flow | Financial risk view | High | Supply Exhibit 99.4 of the Form 40-F |

| June 30, 2026 interim notes not supplied; debt register and maturities dated March 31, 2026 | Refinancing wall and series detail one quarter old | Liquidity and refinancing view | Medium | Supply the June 30, 2026 interim statements |

| Credit agreements, indentures, guarantee and Terrion terms not supplied | Covenant robustness, structural position and loss given default cannot be assessed | Structure view | High | Supply executed agreements and partnership terms |
| Named ratings, outlooks and agency treatment of junior subordinated notes not supplied | The equity credit underpins reported leverage | Leverage view | Medium | Supply agency reports |

| Asset sale terms and any event after July 31, 2026, including third-quarter 2026 results, not supplied | Deleveraging path cannot be quantified | Deleveraging view | High | Supply later filings and agreements |
| Annual information form and holders above a threshold not supplied | Ownership and control cannot be stated | Business risk view | Medium | Supply Exhibit 99.3 and ownership disclosure |
| Operating indicator discrepancies (connection counts, healthcare lives covered) unreconciled | Operating trends are not reliable | Revenue visibility | Minor | Obtain the issuer's reconciliation |
## Next module

CP-5 (evidence trace validator) is next. It should confirm that each figure restated here matches CP-1 and CP-1A, that the equity-credit, covenant-definition, fiscal year 2025 assembly and March 31, 2026 debt-register limits travel with the conclusions, and that the open discrepancies are not used as support.
